What changes

Same six labs, same Bongo recordings. Students find everything in one place, test their setup before the first lab, and get clear, counted requirements. Click a tile to see why; click again to turn it back.

Behind the scenes

Before→After

Structure

  • LAB folderBefore: A Start Here module plus overview and lab pages→After: One LAB folder, no subfolders: a tabbed description, Lab 0, then each lab in Bongo
  • RequirementsBefore: Hidden in drop-downs students have to open→After: On the Bongo page, always visible, with counts
  • DesignBefore: Older blue pages with pop-ups→After: The Spanish layout with French colors, flags and type

Lab 0

  • Guidelines QuizBefore: No quiz on the lab rules→After: A French quiz that unlocks the labs, with three typed accent questions
  • Lab 0Before: First screen recording happens on a due date→After: A one-minute Bongo camera + screen check, due before Lab 1. Both 0%
  • AccentsBefore: No help typing French→After: A keyboard demo for Windows and Mac, with typing practice

Vocabulary

  • AudioBefore: No audio on the word lists→After: Each word links to Forvo, with a ▶ button as a backup

Recording

  • TroubleshootingBefore: A short general list→After: Split into video labs and slide labs, each with one backup: a phone take, or a PowerPoint or Canva MP4
  • Lab 4Before: “The UNG campus,” with an online side note→After: Gainesville or Dahlonega, with photo cards and 3 slides
  • Lab 5Before: Dahlonega only, 4–5 stops→After: Dahlonega, Gainesville or the student's own town, 3 stops with slides
  • Lab 6Before: A practice page: students pick 5 of 47 questions, then record one video→After: A Bongo Question & Answer with 10 recorded questions, 2–3 minutes in all
  • Lab 5 futur procheBefore: “Use futur proche for 3 plans,” under Weather→After: 2 things you'll do and 1 you won't because of the weather, each about a stop

Discrepancy fixes

  • Video lengthBefore: 1.5–2 minutes on some pages, 2 minutes on others→After: 1.5–2 minutes everywhere
  • PointsBefore: 25 “for completion”; the rubric totals 20→After: 20 points, scored with the rubric
  • ResourcesBefore: “Textbook only” and also WordReference.com→After: Class notes, Bonjour à Tous, WordReference.com
  • Lab 6 labelBefore: “Labs 1–5,” but it covers six chapters→After: “Ch. 1–6”
  • Lab 5 mapBefore: “The Dahlonega map,” but no map on the page→After: A map link for the chosen town
  • Lab 4 wordsBefore: “Buildings” required, with one building word given→After: Campus words listed and glossed
  • Lab 5 directionsBefore: Allez tout droit→After: Continuez tout droit

Behind the scenes

  • New GitHub repositoryBefore: Older pages in the fren1001 repository→After: A new fren1001-instructions repository, with Gainesville and Dahlonega copies
  • Course linksBefore: Links tied to one course number→After: Links that survive a course copy
  • Course copyBefore: Copying a course brings last semester's lab items→After: Leave the lab items out; the Lab sets up fresh ones

What stays the same

  • Six regular-session labs, four in summer, five in the full summer session.
  • Individual Bongo videos, with no mini-quizzes.
  • Wednesday 11:59 PM due time.
  • The five-row rubric.

Student workflow

Students go from the announcement to one LAB folder, complete Lab 0 (the Guidelines Quiz and a Bongo setup check), then work through the labs in order. Click a step to see its page.

Previews show the Gainesville copy. Each campus gets its own copy that shows only its own Language Lab contact.

Lab 0: Bongo setup check New

Lab 0 has two parts. Part 1 is the Guidelines Quiz. Part 2 is this one-minute camera + screen recording with three PowerPoint slides, in the first week. Labs 4 and 5 use the screen, so one test covers every lab.

For students

  • Unlimited tries, 0% of the grade.
  • Marked Complete or Not yet within one business day.
  • If screen sharing fails, they practice the fallback: a PowerPoint recording uploaded as an MP4.
  • Stays open all semester to test a new computer.

In D2L

  • Both parts are grade items in the Lab Assignments category, excluded from the final grade. The Bongo check is 1 point: Complete = 1.
  • Every Bongo assignment gets two release conditions: Guidelines Quiz ≥ 75% and Bongo setup check = 1.
  • Bongo needs a 0 option in the Lab 0 rubric (Not yet) to send a 0 to D2L.

Content › LAB › Lab 0 (Bongo)

Lab assignments

What students see when they open each recording in Bongo: the task, vocabulary, troubleshooting, and (in person) how to record in the Lab.

Content › LAB › Lab N Bongo

Lab rubric

The current rubric stays. Five rows at 4 points each, for 20 points per lab.

Content 4Vocabulary 4Grammar 4Fluency / Delivery 4Pronunciation 4

Content 4 points

  1. Excellent4All elements; answers all questions; develops answers beyond expectations.
  2. Good3All elements; answers all questions adequately.
  3. Average2One element missing, or a question unanswered, or answers without details.
  4. Needs improvement1Two or more elements missing, or only 1–2 questions answered, or yes/no answers.
  5. Insufficient0Video is missing, or student answers in English.

Vocabulary 4 points

  1. Excellent4Wide variety (8–10 different words), relevant to the topic; may use effective circumlocution.
  2. Good3A variety (5–7 different words), relevant to the topic.
  3. Average2Some words (fewer than 5), repetitive, or not always relevant.
  4. Needs improvement1Same words repeated, meaning often obscured, or jumps to English.
  5. Insufficient0Speaks English.

Grammar 4 points

  1. Excellent4Exceptional control; accurate most of the time; corrects themselves.
  2. Good3Some mistakes that don't affect meaning (agreement, conjugation, articles).
  3. Average2A few serious mistakes that may change meaning (subject, tense, word order).
  4. Needs improvement1Meaning often obscured; poor control of grammar concepts.
  5. Insufficient0Meaning completely obscured, speaks English, or reads a script with advanced grammar not studied in class.

Fluency / Delivery 4 points

  1. Excellent4Smooth, continuous speech; few long pauses; doesn't read from a script.
  2. Good3Some hesitation or long pauses; doesn't read from a script.
  3. Average2Choppy or slow, with frequent pauses; doesn't read from a script.
  4. Needs improvement1Disjointed; doesn't finish sentences; might read from a script.
  5. Insufficient0Obviously reads from a script.

Pronunciation 4 points

  1. Excellent4Correct pronunciation and intonation; easily understood.
  2. Good3Some mistakes (nasals, final consonants, final E, -tion); meaning not affected.
  3. Average2Pronounced accent; requires sympathetic listening or guessing.
  4. Needs improvement1Meaning often obscured by pronunciation.
  5. Insufficient0Not rated above 0.

All listed elements earn 3 in Content. Only answers that go beyond the task earn 4.

  • The rubric is unchanged. Lab pages now show 20 points to match it.
  • Counted requirements let graders check the Content row directly.

Copying your course to a new semester New

When you copy last semester's course into the new one, leave the lab items out. The Language Lab sets up the LAB folder, its files and the Bongo links in every new course. Copying last semester's lab items creates duplicates and Bongo links that point to old assignments.

  1. In the new course: Course Admin › Import / Export / Copy Components › Copy Components from another Org Unit. Search for your old course, then choose Select Components.

  2. Choose components: set them as shown, then choose Continue.

  3. D2L then shows one page for each component you set to individual items. On each page, uncheck the lab items:

    1. Select Content Modules and Topics: Uncheck the LAB folder. Its name depends on the section type; uncheck whichever shows. Continue.

    2. Select Course Files: Uncheck the lab files folder, whichever shows. Continue.

    3. External Learning Tool Links: Uncheck the lab links: the Bongo lab assignments. Keep any links of your own. Continue.

    4. Grades: Uncheck the Lab Assignments category. Its grade items uncheck with it. Continue.

    5. Quizzes: Uncheck the lab quizzes. Continue.

  4. Finish the copy as usual.
